source_text:
28 ὁμολογεῖ, πρῶτα μὲν ὡς χλεύη τοῖς

πολλοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ προὔκειτο, ἔπειτα δὲ ὅτι καὶ τοῖς
συνεπισκόποις καὶ συλλειτουργοῖς συμβουλεύσας ταῦτα περιαιρεθῆναι οὐκ ἠκούσθη.
εὕρομεν ἐν τῷ τέλει τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ἔμφασιν τοιάδε περιέχουσαν· ὅτι πολλάκις
λαλήσας τοῖς συλλειτουργοῖς μου περιαιρεθῆναι τὰς εἰκόνας οὐκ ἐδέχθην παρ'
αὐτῶν οὐδὲ πρὸς βραχὺ ἀκοῦσαι τῆς ἐμῆς φωνῆς ἠνέσχοντο. 29 ὅπως τὰ βῆλα τὰ
ἔχοντα τοιαύτην γραφὴν συλλεγέντα εἰς ταφὴν τῶν πτωχῶν προχωρήσειεν, τὰ δὲ ἐν
τοίχοις διὰ χρωμάτων λευκανθῆναι.
30 Τὰ δὲ ἐν μουσαρίῳ προληφθέντα γραφῆναι, ἐπειδὴ δυσχερές ἐστι τὸ
τοιοῦτον ἀνασκεύασμα, εἰ μὲν δυνατὸν ἀνασκευασθῆναι, καλόν· εἰ δὲ ἀδύνατον,
ἀρκεσθῆναι τοῖς προγεγονόσι καὶ μηκέτι τινὰ ζωγραφεῖν οὕτως.
thought_title: Epiphanius's requests were mocked and ignored
orientation: Epiphanius is closing his letter by reporting how his advice to remove images was received and restating his final requests about the curtains, wall paintings, and shrine images.
pass_a_gloss: he admits, first that as mockery to the many on the things babbled by him it was set before them, then that also having advised the fellow bishops and fellow ministers that these things be removed he was not listened to. we found at the end of the letter an indication containing such things: that often having spoken to my fellow ministers that the images be removed I was not received by them nor did they endure to hear my voice even for a little. so that the curtains having such a painting being gathered for burial of the poor might go forward, and the things on walls through colors be whitewashed. The things in a shrine previously undertaken to be painted, since difficult is such a removal, if indeed possible to be removed, good; but if impossible, to be content with the things that have already happened and no longer to paint anyone in this way.

choices.term: ὡς χλεύη τοῖς πολλοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ προὔκειτο
choices.english: as mockery to the many on the things babbled by him it was set before them
choices.why: Keeps the passive force of προὔκειτο and the dative of disadvantage τοῖς πολλοῖς, preserving the sense that his words were exposed as a joke to the crowd.
rejected: he was mocked by the many for his babbling

choices.why: Passive aorist of ἀκούω with the sense of being heeded; keeps the passive construction of the source.
rejected: they did not listen to him

choices.term: οὐδὲ πρὸς βραχὺ ἀκοῦσαι τῆς ἐμῆς φωνῆς ἠνέσχοντο
choices.english: nor did they endure to hear my voice even for a little
choices.why: Preserves the strong verb ἠνέσχοντο (endured) and the phrase πρὸς βραχύ (even for a little), showing the complete refusal.
rejected: they would not even briefly listen to me

choices.why: Optative of purpose after ὅπως, keeping the wish/purpose force of the clause.

choices.english: to be content with the things that have already happened
choices.why: Keeps the passive infinitive ἀρκεσθῆναι and the perfect participle προγεγονόσι, preserving the sense of accepting what has already been done.
rejected: to be satisfied with what was already done

choices.english: no longer to paint anyone in this way
choices.why: Keeps the indefinite τινὰ (anyone) and the adverb οὕτως (in this way), preserving the prohibition against future painting of such images.
rejected: to paint no more such images

pass_b_english: He admits that at first his words were set before the many as mockery, on account of the nonsense he babbled, and then that when he advised his fellow bishops and fellow ministers to have these images removed, he was not listened to. We found at the end of the letter an indication containing this: that after speaking many times to my fellow ministers about removing the images, I was not heeded by them, nor did they endure to hear my voice even for a little.
He asks that the curtains bearing such painting be gathered and go forward for the burial of the poor, and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed.

As for the images already painted in the shrine, since such a removal is difficult, if it is possible to remove them, that is good; but if it is impossible, to be content with what has already happened and no longer to paint anyone in this way.

problems.quote: and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed with colors
problems.source_quote: τὰ δὲ ἐν τοίχοις διὰ χρωμάτων λευκανθῆναι
problems.why: English omits 'διὰ χρωμάτων' (with colors). The source specifies whitewashing WITH colors, which is paradoxical and significant — Epiphanius means covering painted images with white paint.
problems.fix: and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed over with colors
problems.ruling: English 'whitewashed with colors' includes διὰ χρωμάτων; no omission. Checker's claim is wrong.

edits.old: and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed with colors.
edits.new: and that the paintings on the walls be whitewashed over with colors.

fixed: Added 'over' to 'whitewashed with colors' to reflect the source's 'διὰ χρωμάτων λευκανθῆναι' (whitewashed with colors), making clear the images are covered over with white paint.

problems.why: λευκαίνω means 'whiten/whitewash', not paint with colors; colors contradict the sense.
problems.ruling: διὰ χρωμάτων modifies λευκανθῆναι: 'whitened by means of colors' is odd; likely 'with paint/pigment' but 'colors' misleads as multicolored, contradicting 'whiten'

problems.quote: on account of the things he babbled
problems.why: 'ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ' is passive: things babbled/spoken against him, not things he babbled.
problems.fix: on account of the nonsense babbled against me
problems.ruling: ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ is passive 'babbled against him,' not 'things he babbled'; reverses agency.

edits.old: on account of the things he babbled
edits.new: on account of the nonsense babbled against him

fixed: Changed 'on account of the things he babbled' to 'on account of the nonsense babbled against him': the source ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ is passive, meaning things babbled against him, not things he babbled.
Changed 'be whitewashed over with colors' to 'be whitewashed': λευκανθῆναι means to whiten or whitewash, not to paint with colors.

problems.quote: I was not received by them
problems.why: Here ἐδέχθην means 'I was not listened to/obeyed,' not 'received'; context is refusal to heed advice.
problems.fix: I was not heeded by them
problems.ruling: οὐκ ἐδέχθην in context means 'I was not accepted/heeded,' not 'received'; parallel to ἠνέσχοντο confirms.

problems.quote: on account of the nonsense babbled against him
problems.why: ληρῳδουμένοις is passive, 'things babbled/nonsense spoken by him,' not 'against him'; agency reversed.
problems.fix: on account of the nonsense he babbled
problems.ruling: ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ is passive 'babbled to him,' not 'against him'; agency/direction reversed.

edits.old: I was not received by them
edits.new: I was not heeded by them

edits.old: on account of the nonsense babbled against him
edits.new: on account of the nonsense he babbled

fixed: Changed 'I was not received by them' to 'I was not heeded by them' because ἐδέχθην here means 'I was not listened to/obeyed,' not 'received.'
Changed 'on account of the nonsense babbled against him' to 'on account of the nonsense he babbled' because ληρῳδουμένοις is passive, meaning things babbled by him, not against him.

refereed.quote: He admits that at first his words were set before the many as mockery, on account of the nonsense he babbled
refereed.source_quote: ὁμολογεῖ, πρῶτα μὲν ὡς χλεύη τοῖς πολλοῖς ἐπὶ τοῖς ληρῳδουμένοις αὐτῷ προὔκειτο
refereed.why: Subject confusion: source says 'it' (the letter/image matter) was set as mockery, not 'his words'.
refereed.fix: He admits that at first it was set before the many as mockery, on account of the nonsense babbled about him.
refereed.ruling: προὔκειτο has no explicit subject; 'his words' adds a subject not in source, potentially misleading readers about what was mocked.
